title: A low-salt week for blood pressure and weight
summary: Fourteen simple meals that cut salt, add fiber and keep saturated fat low, written for a Thermomix with real settings. Every claim below was read by the review board against public sources.

recipes.title: Lentil and vegetable soup
steps: Chop onion, carrot and garlic: 5 sec / speed 5.
Sauté with 1 tsp olive oil: 3 min / 120°C / speed 1.
Add 250 g lentils and 900 ml low-sodium stock.
Cook: 30 min / 100°C / reverse / speed 1.
Finish with herbs and pepper, no salt.
recipes.why: Lentils bring fiber and plant protein with no added salt, in line with cutting sodium.
recipes.evidence: On average, adults who keep salt under 5 g a day (about 2 g of sodium) have lower blood pressure [WHO — Sodium reduction].

recipes.title: Steamed salmon with broccoli and brown rice
steps: Chop garlic and herbs: 3 sec / speed 5.
Put the grain in the simmering basket; fill the bowl with 900 ml water (no salt).
Fish or chicken on the Varoma tray, vegetables in the Varoma dish; season with herbs, lemon and pepper, not salt.
Steam: 25 min / Varoma / speed 1.
Plate with a teaspoon of olive oil; the grain from the basket on the side.
recipes.why: Oily fish and vegetables, seasoned with lemon instead of salt, for the pressure goal.
recipes.evidence: On average, adults who keep salt under 5 g a day (about 2 g of sodium) have lower blood pressure [WHO — Sodium reduction].

recipes.title: Chickpea, tomato and spinach bowl
steps: Quinoa in the basket, 700 ml water: 15 min / 100°C / speed 1.
Meanwhile rinse the chickpeas (no-salt-added can).
Mix quinoa, chickpeas, halved tomatoes and raw spinach.
Dress with lemon, 1 tsp olive oil and pepper.
recipes.why: Legumes and whole grain give fiber; the no-salt-added can keeps sodium low.
recipes.evidence: On average, people who eat at least 400 g of fruit and vegetables a day have a lower risk of chronic disease [WHO — Healthy diet].

recipes.title: Chicken breast with zucchini and bell peppers
steps: Chop garlic and herbs: 3 sec / speed 5.
Put the grain in the simmering basket; fill the bowl with 900 ml water (no salt).
Fish or chicken on the Varoma tray, vegetables in the Varoma dish; season with herbs, lemon and pepper, not salt.
Steam: 22 min / Varoma / speed 1.
Plate with a teaspoon of olive oil; the grain from the basket on the side.
recipes.why: Lean protein and two vegetables, steamed so no fat is added.
recipes.evidence: On average, keeping saturated fat below 10% of daily energy is associated with better heart health [WHO — Healthy diet].

recipes.title: Oat and Greek yogurt bowl with blueberries
steps: Soak 60 g oats in 150 ml milk or water for 10 min (or overnight).
Top with 150 g Greek yogurt, blueberries, sliced banana and a few walnuts.
No sugar added: the fruit sweetens it.
recipes.why: Whole oats, fruit and unsalted nuts: fiber and unsaturated fat without added sugar.
recipes.evidence: On average, keeping free sugars below 10% of daily energy lowers the risk of unhealthy weight gain [WHO — Healthy diet].

steps: Chop garlic and herbs: 3 sec / speed 5.
Put the grain in the simmering basket; fill the bowl with 900 ml water (no salt).
Fish or chicken on the Varoma tray, vegetables in the Varoma dish; season with herbs, lemon and pepper, not salt.
Steam: 20 min / Varoma / speed 1.
Plate with a teaspoon of olive oil; the grain from the basket on the side.
recipes.why: White fish, low in saturated fat, with vegetables and a whole grain.
recipes.evidence: On average, keeping saturated fat below 10% of daily energy is associated with better heart health [WHO — Healthy diet].

recipes.title: Whole-wheat pasta with tomato, spinach and ricotta
steps: Chop garlic: 3 sec / speed 5; sauté with 1 tsp oil: 2 min / 120°C / speed 1.
Add halved tomatoes: 8 min / 100°C / reverse / speed 1.
Cook 80 g whole-wheat pasta separately (no salt in the water); drain.
Toss pasta with the sauce, raw spinach and 50 g ricotta; pepper.
recipes.why: Whole-wheat pasta for fiber; ricotta gives protein with less saturated fat than hard cheese.
recipes.evidence: On average, people who eat at least 400 g of fruit and vegetables a day have a lower risk of chronic disease [WHO — Healthy diet].

steps: Chop garlic and herbs: 3 sec / speed 5.

Fish or chicken on the Varoma tray, vegetables in the Varoma dish; season with herbs, lemon and pepper, not salt.

recipes.title: Cannellini bean and tuna-free salad
steps: Rinse the beans (no-salt-added can).
Slice onion thin: 3 sec / speed 4.
Mix beans, tomatoes, onion and spinach; lemon, 1 tsp oil, pepper.
recipes.why: A no-cook legume salad: fiber and plant protein, no added salt.
recipes.evidence: On average, people who eat at least 400 g of fruit and vegetables a day have a lower risk of chronic disease [WHO — Healthy diet].

steps: Chop garlic and herbs: 3 sec / speed 5.

Fish or chicken on the Varoma tray, vegetables in the Varoma dish; season with herbs, lemon and pepper, not salt.

recipes.title: Tofu, broccoli and brown rice bowl
steps: Rice in the basket, 900 ml water: 25 min / 100°C / speed 1.
Tofu cubes and broccoli in the Varoma for the last 15 min.
Dress with vinegar, garlic, 1 tsp oil and pepper.
recipes.why: Plant protein and a cruciferous vegetable; no soy sauce, to keep sodium down.
recipes.evidence: On average, adults who keep salt under 5 g a day (about 2 g of sodium) have lower blood pressure [WHO — Sodium reduction].

recipes.title: Egg and vegetable frittata (oven)
steps: Chop vegetables: 5 sec / speed 5.
Sauté with 1 tsp oil: 5 min / 120°C / speed 1.
Beat 3 eggs with herbs and pepper (no salt); mix in the vegetables.
Oven dish, 180°C for 20 min.
recipes.why: Eggs with plenty of vegetables, herbs instead of salt.
recipes.evidence: On average, people who eat at least 400 g of fruit and vegetables a day have a lower risk of chronic disease [WHO — Healthy diet].

recipes.title: Chicken and vegetable soup
steps: Chop vegetables: 5 sec / speed 5.
Add 800 ml low-sodium stock and diced chicken: 20 min / 100°C / reverse / speed 1.
Add 60 g small whole-wheat pasta: 10 min / 100°C / reverse / speed 1.
Pepper and herbs, no salt.
recipes.why: A low-sodium stock makes a comforting soup that fits the pressure goal.
recipes.evidence: On average, adults who keep salt under 5 g a day (about 2 g of sodium) have lower blood pressure [WHO — Sodium reduction].

recipes.title: Baked cod with cherry tomatoes and lentils
steps: Lentils: 200 g in the bowl with 700 ml water, 25 min / 100°C / reverse / speed 1.
Cod and tomatoes in an oven dish with garlic, lemon and 1 tsp oil: 180°C for 15 min.
Serve the cod over the lentils; pepper, no salt.
recipes.why: Fish and legumes together: protein, fiber and little saturated fat.
recipes.evidence: On average, keeping saturated fat below 10% of daily energy is associated with better heart health [WHO — Healthy diet].

movement: Tue: stairs instead of the lift, every time; 20-minute walk.
Wed: 30-minute walk; 10 minutes of light strength (chair squats, wall push-ups).
Sat: a longer walk, 45-60 minutes, somewhere you like.
Sun: rest, or a gentle 20-minute walk.
